questions.question: Describe how the uprising spread across the country in 1976.
questions.expected_answer: 17 June: Alexandra, Kagiso, Tembisa; East and West Rand; Pretoria townships (Atteridgeville, Mamelodi). Universities: Zululand (18 June buildings burned), Turfloop (closed), Fort Hare. Some Wits students marched in solidarity. SSRC formed (Mashinini). Cape Town: 11 August Langa, Gugulethu, Nyanga; coloured students from Bonteheuwel, Athlone, Manenberg and UWC joined; early September march in city centre; some Indian students. Eastern Cape (Port Elizabeth, New Brighton, East London), Free State, homelands; more than a hundred towns; uneven spread; cycle of funerals and clashes.

questions.question: Explain the stay-aways and community campaigns.
questions.expected_answer: SSRC wanted worker support. Stay-aways: 4-6 August (Johannesburg); 23-25 August, Mzimhlophe hostel clashes (lost wages, students' force, evidence of police encouragement, dozens killed); SSRC met hostel dwellers; 13-15 September most successful, hundreds of thousands stayed away, Cape Town too. Campaigns: against shebeens and beer halls; no Christmas celebrations December 1976; 1977 rent increase stopped; Urban Bantu Council resigned; exam boycotts. Leaders: Mashinini fled August 1976, Seatlholo, Montsisi arrested June 1977.

questions.question: Explain the government's response and the different responses within communities.
questions.expected_answer: Vorster and Kruger blamed agitators and communists; thousands detained without trial (Internal Security Act, Terrorism Act); Mapetla Mohapi died in custody August 1976; schools closed; meetings banned. Cillié Commission: 575 dead June 1976-February 1977, about 3 900 injured, most killed by police; real figure possibly higher; blamed agitators and BC but noted Afrikaans and conditions. Communities: Black Parents' Association (Winnie Mandela, Nthato Motlana); some parents feared for safety and schooling; some workers supported, others resented or were intimidated; mixed homeland responses. UN Security Council condemnation 19 June 1976; anti-apartheid movements grew.
